extracted.intended_audience: NIH reviewers and computational structural biologists / molecular modelers designing membrane-protein inhibitors
extracted.subtask_description: Computational construction, refinement, validation of atomic-resolution EmrE membrane-protein structures and in silico design/optimization of proteolysis-resistant peptide dimerization inhibitors, with downstream experimental testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1: Construct and validate an atomic-level model of EmrE
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct and validate an atomic-level model of the EmrE membrane protein. The Cα structures will be used with available modeling protocols to construct a series of all-atom models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve models by molecular dynamics simulations with replica exchange in the presence of an explicit lipid membrane and water; compute free energy of refined structural candidates with the confinement method; select lowest-free-energy candidates and validate by comparison with experimentally determined ligand dissociation constants and residue pKa values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2: Design peptide analogues to inhibit EmrE dimerization
rubrics_metrics.description: To design peptide analogues that inactivate the EmrE transporter by preventing dimerization, mimicking TM4 and optimizing sequence to bind the EmrE monomer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial inhibitor model identical to TM4; optimize peptide sequence based on interaction energies between EmrE monomer and peptide; model proteolysis-resistant all-hydrocarbon stapled α-helical peptides; iterate MD-based optimization and synthesize/test best candidates experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple side-chain modeling algorithms to generate initial all-atom models
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting from Cα coordinates, generate coordinates of backbone and side chains using several algorithms (SCWRL, OPUS-Rota, SCMF, ROSETTA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate backbone via CHARMM internal coordinates and apply dihedral restraints to keep φ/ψ in allowed Ramachandran regions; energy-minimize with CHARMM using an implicit membrane model; detect and correct any chirality errors before MD refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine modeled structures by MD in explicit lipid bilayer with explicit solvent/ions
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert modeled structures into pre-equilibrated DPMC lipid bilayers with explicit water and ions and perform MD to refine structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CHARMM-GUI for insertion; run equilibrium MD with ACE-MD on GPUs and NAMD; typical system ~50,000 atoms; expect several hundred nanoseconds to reach steady-state; CHARMM/NAMD/AceMD protocols described for equilibration and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply enhanced-sampling methods (temperature REMD and LES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use temperature replica exchange MD (REMD) and Locally Enhanced Sampling (LES) to accelerate conformational sampling for membrane protein refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct REMD across temperatures from 300K up to ~600K (only 300K used for evaluation); perform LES with CHARMM (implicit solvent) and NAMD (explicit solvent); use variable restraints to transform LES ensemble into proper canonical ensemble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate refined structures by fit to experimental electron density (EM) maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether MD-refined coordinates fit experimental EM density maps and perform additional MD with restraints to the EM map if coordinates do not fit completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain final structures whose coordinates are consistent with the EM map for further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank candidate structures by configurational free energy via implicit-membrane + confinement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove explicit lipids/waters, place structures into an implicit membrane model and estimate solvation free energy and protein configurational free energy using a confinement analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain lowest-free-energy structures; if several distinct structures have very similar free energies, retain all for further validation and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute ligand binding free energies using alchemical annihilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the free energy (FE) of ligand binding (e.g., TPP+, ethidium) by reversible alchemical annihilation in both the EmrE active site and in aqueous/lipid solvent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameterize ligands using CHARMM-CGENFF (with QM/MM iterative improvement per CHARMM protocol); perform alchemical FE calculations with NAMD and analyze with VMD; use standard alchemical FE best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine pKa’s of key residues to validate active-site arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate pKa shifts for residues involved in transport (e.g., Glu14) using Poisson-Boltzmann solvation theory and alchemical free-energy simulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare predicted pKa values to experimental literature values (e.g., Glu-14 literature 7.3–8.5); perform alchemical protonation calculations to compute pKa shifts as a stringent test of active-site structural quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use initial EmrE–peptide inhibition models that isolate TM4
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct two EmrE–peptide starting models by deleting all parts of one monomer except TM4 (and vice versa) to create monomer–peptide complexes for simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform MD equilibration of monomer–peptide complexes (100 ns) and also simulate the isolated TM4 peptide in the bilayer (100 ns) to normalize interaction energies; use lowest-average-interaction-energy trajectory as starting point for mutational optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize peptide sequence via Monte Carlo using interaction-energy differences (∆E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select residues near the monomer interface, mutate randomly to nonpolar residues and evaluate change in interaction energy ∆E = E_complex_mutated − E_complex_original − (E_peptide_mutated − E_peptide_original).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Metropolis acceptance: Paccept = 1 if ∆E ≤ 0, else exp(−β∆E); vary β (inverse temperature) from physiological to higher values to broaden sampling; repeat until composition stabilizes; each trial evaluated by repeating 100 ns MD of complex and peptide-alone simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include peptide–lipid interaction energies when assessing binding in membrane environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Because binding occurs in the membrane, account for interaction energies between peptide and lipid both in bound and free states in the ∆E calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute interaction energies from MD trajectories of peptide in complex and peptide alone in membrane to normalize membrane contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate error from neglecting entropy by computing binding free energy and enthalpy differences via confinement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The optimization protocol uses interaction-energy differences (enthalpy-like) instead of full free energies; quantify entropic contribution/error using confinement analysis with an implicit membrane model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform confinement-based calculations to compute binding free energy and enthalpy differences resulting from a trial mutation to assess magnitude of neglected entropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design proteolysis-resistant stapled peptide analogs with staples placed away from binding interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct stapled all-hydrocarbon α-helical peptides (staple positions among residue pairs separated by 3, 4 or 7 residues) that mimic TM4 sequence but resist proteolysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only consider staple positions away from the protein-binding interface; use TM4 reference sequence positions (84–105) as candidate locations; replace sidechains with hydrocarbon staples and simulate stapled peptides in complex and alone to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank stapled peptide candidates by interaction-energy differences and α-helical propensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank candidates based on the computed interaction energy differences (peptide–protein and peptide–lipid) and the peptide’s α-helical propensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain highest-scoring stapled peptides for experimental characterization (synthesis and efflux inhibition assays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameterize small-molecule ligands with CHARMM-CGENFF following CHARMM protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit ligand coordinates to CHARMM-CGENFF to generate force field parameters and iteratively improve with alternating quantum and molecular-mechanical calculations per CHARMM parametrization protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is standard computational chemistry procedure and necessary prior to alchemical FE calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow best practices in free-energy calculations and alchemical protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply established methods for absolute and relative binding free-energy calculations (alchemical annihilation, restraining potentials) and adhere to good-practice recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use references and protocols (Boresch et al., Wang et al., Shirts, Pohorille et al.) and standard analysis workflows for reliable FE results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use realistic membrane composition known to support EmrE function (DPMC used here)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert models into DPMC lipid bilayers (EmrE known to be functional in DPMC) though other membrane compositions may be used if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHARMM-GUI used to build mixed bilayers; choose membrane composition consistent with biological activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage experimental collaborators for synthesis and functional testing of designed peptides
rubrics_metrics.description: Validated in silico peptide analogs should be synthesized and tested experimentally by collaborators (e.g., synthesis and efflux inhibition assays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of support from synthesis/experimental labs indicated; plan for experimental testing within the two-year project period for top candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline expectations for deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated pacing: ~6 months to produce several refined structures (Aims 1a–1c), additional 4–6 months for validation (Aims 1c–1d), remaining time for peptide optimization and stapling (Aim 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and iterative cycles between in silico optimization and experimental testing are expected to be completed within the two-year R03 period for at least some candidate peptides.
